title: Sheaves of abelian groups and of modules
statement:
For a scheme $T$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ be the abelian category of sheaves of abelian groups on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] $T_{\Et}$; a sheaf of abelian groups is as in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck; def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For a commutative ring $R$, let $R_T$ be the constant sheaf of rings on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and write $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ for the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

A sheaf $F\in\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is *torsion* if every local section is locally killed by a positive integer: for every object $U\to T$ and $s\in F(U)$ there are an etale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $n_i>0$ with $n_i(s|_{U_i})=0$.

A sheaf of sets on $T_{\Et}$ means an object of $\Sh(T_{\Et})$ as defined in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Such a sheaf $F$ is *locally constant* if there is an etale covering $\{U_i\to T\}$ such that, for each $i$, its restriction along the induced functor $(U_i)_{\Et}\to T_{\Et}$ (without further sheafification) is isomorphic to a constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. It is *finite locally constant* if it is locally constant and every geometric stalk $F_{\bar t}$ at every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], with stalks defined in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], is a finite set; *lisse* means finite locally constant.

A sheaf $F$ is *constructible* if $T$ has a finite stratification by locally closed subschemes $(\iota_k:Z_k\to T)_{k<n}$ [def-constructible-stratification] such that each underlying subset is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset] and, for every $k$, the restriction $\iota_k^{-1}F$ is finite locally constant. Here $\iota_k^{-1}F$ denotes the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf pullback of $F$ along the base-change functor $T_{\Et}\to (Z_k)_{\Et}$, $V\mapsto V\times_T Z_k$ (the presheaf $W\mapsto\operatorname{colim}_{W\to V\times_TZ_k}F(V)$).

Finally, for an object $K$ of a derived category of sheaves, say that $K$ has *torsion cohomology* if every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^r(K)$, defined by the cohomology-sheaf construction [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], is a torsion sheaf in the preceding sense.
